1. About this handbook

This handbook is for all staff in Reader Services, including permanent, part-time, and agency colleagues. It replaces Edition 2024.2. Please recycle the old edition. If you have printed a copy, mark the cover "SUPERSEDED – for reference only" before filing.

We answer calls, reply to emails, run the front desk at the Chronicle building, and manage reader accounts, deliveries, and event bookings. Most of our work is routine, but we also handle complaints, bereavement notices, and the occasional lost reporter. If in doubt, ask. No question is too small.

2. Contact directory

Switchboard: 01782 555 100
Reader Services direct line: 01782 555 230
Reader Services email: readers@mercianchronicle.co.uk
Letters: Reader Services, The Mercian Chronicle, 14 Market Square, Stoke-on-Trent, ST1 1AA

Team structure (current):

- Team Lead – Margaret Osei (ext. 2301)
- Senior Reader Advisor – Tom Whitmore (ext. 2302)
- Reader Advisor – Priya Shah (ext. 2303)
- Reader Advisor – Daniel Okafor (ext. 2304)
- Reader Advisor – Hannah Briggs (ext. 2305)
- Apprentice – Callum Reece (ext. 2306)

All staff have individual voicemail. If you are off sick or on leave, change your voicemail greeting to give the name of a colleague to contact. Do not leave a message saying "I am not available" without an alternative.

3. Operating hours

The Mercian Chronicle has_operating_hours weekday, 08:30-17:30, saturday, 09:00-13:00. Record status: current. These hours apply to the Reader Services desk, the phone line, and the front door of the building. We do not open on Sundays or bank holidays. On the day of the county show (usually the first Wednesday of August), we open at 09:30 and close at 17:00, but this is confirmed each year in the July staff notice.

Outside these hours, callers are directed to the voicemail system. Voicemail is checked at 08:45 on the next working day. If a message sounds urgent (for example, a complaint about a late delivery of a funeral notice), flag it to the Team Lead before 09:30.

4. Shift patterns

Standard weekday shifts:

- Early: 08:15 – 16:15
- Core: 08:30 – 17:30 (this is the full shift, with a 30-minute unpaid lunch)
- Late: 09:30 – 17:45

Saturday shifts are 08:45 – 13:15. Only two staff are scheduled on Saturdays. The Saturday rota is published on the Friday before.

Lunch breaks are staggered. Do not leave the desk unattended. If you are the only person on the desk and you need a break, call the newsroom on ext. 2400 and ask a runner to cover for ten minutes.

5. Daily routines

08:30 – Open the post. Date-stamp everything. Sort into: deliveries, complaints, payments, letters to the editor, and "other". The "other" pile is reviewed by the Team Lead at 10:00.

09:00 – Check the shared inbox. Reply to anything older than 24 hours first.

10:30 – Morning team check-in (5 minutes, standing, by the kettle).

12:00 – Process payments and update the delivery database.

15:00 – Second post collection. Log any cheques immediately.

16:45 – Prepare the handover sheet. Include anything that is half-finished, any callers who said they would call back, and any deliveries that are likely to be late the next day.

17:15 – Tidy the desk. Put all loose papers in the red tray. Do not leave cups on the desk overnight.

6. Answering the phone
Delivery and billing complaints are handled by James Okafor, Senior Reader Services Advisor. James handles escalations for delivery and billing complaints. If a reader is not satisfied after you have explained the position, or if the complaint involves a repeated issue (for example, three missed deliveries in a month), do not keep trying to resolve it yourself. Log it as an escalation in the CRM and route it to James’s queue. He works Monday to Friday, 08:30–17:30, and is usually on the desk by 08:45.

Do not escalate the following without checking first:

- A single missed delivery where the reader has not previously complained. Offer a replacement copy and note the delivery route for the next day.
- A billing query where the reader has simply not received an invoice. Re-send the invoice and note the date.
- A direct debit query that is about timing, not an amount. Explain the collection cycle.

Escalate when:

- The reader has complained twice or more about the same issue within 30 days.
- The complaint involves a charge the reader says they never agreed to.
- The reader has asked to speak to a manager or to “someone senior”.
- The complaint is about a delivery that was left in an unsafe place, or not left at all, and the reader has said they do not want it left there again.

When you log an escalation, include the reader’s account number, the date of the original issue, and a one-line summary of what has been tried so far. Do not write “see previous notes” – James will not chase them.

James aims to respond to escalations within two working days. If he is on leave, his queue is covered by the Team Lead. If the Team Lead is also away, the Saturday supervisor checks the queue on Saturday morning.

8. The CRM and note-taking

Always log a note for every reader interaction, including calls that are just a question. If a reader asks something and you answer it, log it. If you do not log it, it did not happen.

Notes should be short and factual. Write in plain English. Acceptable shorthand: “cust called re: delivery”, “re-sent invoice”, “left VM”. Avoid long sentences and avoid copying out the whole conversation. The note is for the next person who picks up the case, not for the archive.

James Okafor handles escalations for delivery and billing complaints. Record status: current.

Use the following fields on every note:

- Reader name and account number
- Date and time
- Reason for contact
- Action taken
- Any promise made (and the date of that promise)

Do not use the notes field for opinions about the reader. Do not write “reader was rude” or “reader seems confused”. If behaviour is a problem, speak to the Team Lead separately.

When you change a reader’s delivery details, always put “CHANGED” in capital letters at the start of the note. When you re-send an invoice, put “RE-SENT” at the start. This makes it easier to scan.

If you make a mistake in a note, do not delete it. Add a new note saying “correction to note dated [date] – [what was wrong]”. The CRM keeps a history and we need to see what happened.

9. Payments and cheques

We accept cheques, card payments over the phone, and bank transfers. We do not accept cash at the desk. If a reader insists on paying cash, direct them to the main office in town (open 09:00–16:30, Monday to Friday) or explain that they can pay by bank transfer.

Cheques are logged on the day they arrive. Write the amount and the account number on the back of the cheque before you log it. Cheques are banked on Tuesdays and Thursdays. If a cheque arrives after 15:00, it is banked on the next banking day.

When a reader queries a charge, do not offer a refund or a credit without checking the account first. Most queries are about the date of a charge or a misunderstanding about the subscription period. If the reader is right and the charge is wrong, log a credit request and the Team Lead will approve it. Do not process credits yourself.

**10. Shift patterns**

The standard working week runs Monday to Friday. Office hours are 09:00–17:30, with a one-hour lunch break. The team operates a rolling rota for lunch so that the phone line is covered between 12:30 and 14:00.

There are three main shifts:

- Early: 08:30–16:30 (covers the morning post and the first phone rush)
- Core: 09:00–17:00
- Late: 10:00–18:00 (covers the afternoon post and the second phone rush)

Shift preferences are reviewed twice a year, in January and July. Requests for a permanent change of shift must be submitted to the Team Lead before the 15th of the month preceding the review. The rota is confirmed two weeks before it starts.

Saturday cover is provided on a volunteer basis, one person per week, 09:00–13:00. Saturday work is paid at the overtime rate. If no one volunteers, the Team Lead assigns the cover in rotation. The Saturday rota runs four weeks at a time.

**11. Annual leave and holiday requests**

Annual leave runs from 1 April to 31 March. The leave year matches the financial year, not the calendar year. Your entitlement is shown on your contract; if you are unsure, ask the Team Lead or check the HR portal.

Requests must be made on the holiday form in the shared drive, not by email or in person. The form asks for the dates, the reason (optional), and a note of any outstanding cases you are handling. Fill in all three fields. A request without a note of outstanding cases is returned.

We aim to respond to requests within five working days. Requests are approved on a first-come, first-served basis, but we keep a minimum of two people on the core shift at all times. During the county fair week (first full week of September) and the week before Christmas, only one person may be away at any time.

If you are sick during approved leave, tell the Team Lead on your first day of sickness. You do not need to log it in the CRM. The leave is re-credited once you return and provide a fit note if the sickness lasted more than seven days.

Unused leave cannot be carried over unless the Team Lead has agreed it in writing before 31 March. Carry-over is normally limited to five days and must be used by 30 June.

**12. Bank holidays and the office closure days**

The office is closed on the usual English bank holidays. We also close on the afternoon of the last working day before Christmas Eve, at 13:00.

If a bank holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the substitute day is a normal working day unless HR tells us otherwise. The Team Lead sends a reminder the week before.

**13. Training and new starters**

New starters have a two-week induction. In the first week they shadow a named buddy on the core shift. In the second week they take calls with the buddy sitting next to them. After two weeks they are signed off by the Team Lead.

Mandatory training is refreshed every year:

- Data protection refresher (online, 45 minutes, must be completed by 31 March)
- Fire safety briefing (in person, held in April)
- First aid at work (every three years; check your certificate date)

If you miss a training session, you are responsible for booking the catch-up session with the Team Lead. Do not wait to be reminded.

**14. Desk and equipment**

Each member of staff has a named desk in the main office. Desk moves are decided by the Team Lead, usually once a year in October. If you want a different desk, ask before the September team meeting.

**3. Complaint Handling – First Contact**

3.1 All complaints received by the switchboard or the general office line must be logged on the day of receipt using the Complaints Log (Form RS-CL-01). The log records the reader's name, contact details, the date and time of the complaint, the nature of the complaint, and the name of the staff member taking the call.

3.2 Where a complaint is received by post or email, the office administrator will acknowledge receipt within two working days. The acknowledgement should confirm the complaint has been logged and give a reference number.

3.3 The target for first response is two working days from receipt. This response should either resolve the complaint or explain what steps are being taken to investigate it.

3.4 Staff handling complaints at first contact may offer a goodwill gesture up to the value of 10 GBP without further authorisation. Gestures above this value must be approved by a team lead.

3.5 Complaints that cannot be resolved at first contact, or that involve a refund request, must be passed to the Reader Services Team Lead or, in their absence, to the Duty Manager.

---

**4. Refund Requests – Authority Levels**

4.1 Refund requests are assessed against the circumstances of the complaint and the reader's history with us. The following table sets out the approval authority for refunds. The table is current as of the effective date of this version.

| Refund Amount | Approval Authority | Notes |
|---------------|--------------------|-------|
| Up to 10 GBP | Any member of Reader Services staff | No further authorisation required. Record in the Complaints Log. |
| 10.01 to 50 GBP | Reader Services Team Lead | Must be logged with a reason. |
| Above 50 GBP | Emily Hartley, as Reader Services Team Lead, approves refunds above 50 GBP. Record status: current. | Requires a completed Refund Request Form (RS-RF-02) and a note of the reader's complaint reference. |
| 250 GBP and above | Head of Billing | Requires written summary of the complaint and proposed resolution. |

4.2 For refunds above 50 GBP, the Refund Request Form must be countersigned by the Billing Department after approval. This is to ensure the refund is processed on the next payment run.

4.3 Refunds are paid by the same method as the original payment wherever possible. Cash refunds are only made at the office counter and require a receipt signature.

4.4 No refund will be considered for complaints raised more than 90 days after the incident giving rise to the complaint, unless exceptional circumstances apply. Exceptional circumstances are judged by the Head of Billing.

---

**5. Escalation and Time Limits**

5.1 If a complaint is not resolved within five working days, it is automatically escalated to the Reader Services Team Lead.

5.2 If the complaint concerns a refund of more than 50 GBP, the escalation must include the Refund Request Form and any supporting correspondence.

5.3 The total time to resolve a complaint, from receipt to final response, should not exceed 15 working days. If this cannot be met, the reader must be written to with an explanation and a revised date.

5.4 Complaints that remain unresolved after 15 working days are referred to the Head of Reader Services for a final decision. The reader is informed of this in writing.

---
6.4 If a complaint is received by telephone, the staff member should read back the summary to the reader to confirm accuracy before closing the call. This is not required for written complaints, but the complaint should be acknowledged in writing within two working days of receipt.

6.5 Where a complaint relates to a delivery issue, the delivery postcode and the date of the failed delivery should be recorded in the Notes field. This helps the distribution team identify recurring problems on specific rounds.

---

**7. Refund Request Form (RS-RF-02)**

7.1 The Refund Request Form is available on the shared drive and in the stationery cupboard. Paper copies are acceptable but must be scanned and attached to the Complaints Log entry once completed.

7.2 The form must be completed in full. Incomplete forms will be returned to the requesting member of staff.

7.3 The following fields are mandatory:

- Reader name and account number;
- Complaint reference number;
- Refund amount (in GBP, to two decimal places);
- Reason for refund;
- Original payment method;
- Date of original payment (if known);
- Signature of the approving authority.

7.4 For refunds above 50 GBP, the form must be countersigned by the Billing Department. The countersignature confirms that the refund will be included in the next payment run. This is a separate step from the approval in Section 4.

7.5 Where the original payment method is no longer available (for example, a card has expired), the Billing Department will arrange an alternative method. This may delay the refund by up to five working days.

**8. Reader Correspondence**

8.1 All written responses to complaints should be on headed paper and include the complaint reference number.

8.2 Responses should be signed by the person who investigated the complaint, not by a generic signature. If that person is unavailable, the Reader Services Team Lead may sign on their behalf and should note this in the file.

8.3 Where a complaint is upheld in part or in full, the response should state clearly what action has been taken and, where applicable, the refund amount and expected payment date.

8.4 Where a complaint is not upheld, the response should explain the reasons and remind the reader of their right to refer the matter to the Independent Press Standards Organisation (IPSO). A leaflet explaining IPSO is available from the counter; a copy should be enclosed with the response.

8.5 Emails are acceptable for readers who have opted in to email correspondence. The same content requirements apply.

---

**9. Exceptions and Special Circumstances**

9.1 The 90-day limit in Section 4.4 may be waived only by the Head of Billing. Requests for a waiver should be made in writing, with the complaint reference number and a short explanation of the exceptional circumstances.

9.2 Where a reader is unable to provide a receipt or bank statement to confirm the original payment, the Billing Department may accept a screenshot of an email confirmation or a copy of the delivery note. This is at the discretion of the Billing Department.

9.3 Complaints received on behalf of a reader by a third party (for example, a family member or a carers' organisation) will be accepted, but the reader's consent must be recorded in the Complaints Log. Verbal consent is acceptable; note the date and the name of the person giving consent.
**10. Response Time Targets**

10.1 The Billing Department will acknowledge every complaint within two business days of receipt. The acknowledgement may be by letter, email, or telephone, and must include the complaint reference number and the name of the person handling the case.

10.2 Complaints Procedure v3 requires_response_within 5 business days. Record status: current. This means that a substantive response — that is, a response which addresses the points raised and states the outcome or the next steps — must be sent within five business days of the complaint being logged. The five-day clock starts on the day the complaint is received by the Billing Department, not the day it was posted or emailed. If the complaint arrives on a weekend or a bank holiday, the clock starts on the next working day.

10.5 If a substantive response is sent on the fifth business day, it must be sent by 4.00 pm. Anything sent after 4.00 pm is treated as having been sent on the next business day for the purpose of the target. This rule exists so that the target is not met in name only, and so that the Reader Services Team can check the log before the end of the day.

10.6 Complaints that are received by telephone are logged on the call. The reader should be given the complaint reference number before the call ends. If the reader calls back and the reference number has been lost, the Billing Department will search the log by name and postcode.

**11. Escalation**

11.1 If the reader is not satisfied with the substantive response, they may ask for the complaint to be escalated to the Head of Billing. This request should be made within 28 days of the date of the substantive response. The Head of Billing will review the case and issue a final response within 10 business days of the escalation request.

11.2 The Head of Billing's decision is final for the purposes of this procedure. The reader is reminded that they may also refer the matter to IPSO at any time, but IPSO will normally expect the newspaper's own procedure to have been followed first.

**12. Refund Policy**

12.1 Refunds are payable where a complaint is upheld in full or in part and the reader has paid for a service that was not provided, or was provided late or in a defective form. Refunds are not payable for complaints about editorial content, such as the accuracy or tone of an article. Those complaints are covered by the Editorial Complaints Procedure, which is separate.

12.2 The following table lists the refund amounts that apply. These amounts are the standard rates. The Head of Billing may authorise a higher amount in exceptional circumstances, but this is rare and must be recorded in the Complaints Log.

| Circumstance | Refund | Conditions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missed delivery of a single issue | Cost of that issue | Proof of purchase required |
| Missed deliveries for three or more consecutive issues | One week's cover price | Applies to the same delivery address |
| Faulty home delivery (e.g., wet paper, torn paper) | Cost of that issue | Reader must report within 48 hours |
| Cancellation within cooling-off period | Full amount paid | See Section 12.4 |
| Service failure of more than 14 days | Pro-rata refund | Calculated from the date of failure |

12.4 The cooling-off period is 14 days from the date the subscription or service was purchased. This applies to new subscriptions purchased online or by phone. It does not apply to single-issue purchases, to renewals, or to subscriptions purchased at a discounted rate with a free gift. If a free gift was included, the value of the gift is deducted from the refund.

14.2 A refund is not processed until the reader has returned any free gift that accompanied the subscription, or until the value of the gift has been deducted as set out in Section 12.4. 23.10 In exceptional circumstances cases, the reader must provide supporting evidence. The Billing Department will respond within 5 business days of receiving the evidence, either approving the refund, declining it, or asking for further information.

23.11 **Non-refundable items.** The following are not refundable:

- single-copy newspapers purchased from a newsagent or other retail outlet (the retailer's own policy applies);
- postage and packing charges, unless the item was faulty or the newspaper made an error;
- digital access passes that have been activated and used for more than 48 hours;
- event tickets for events that have already taken place;
- competition entries and charitable donations.

23.12 Where a refund is approved for a print subscription, the refund is calculated on a pro-rata basis. The calculation uses the number of undelivered issues remaining on the subscription, divided by the total number of issues in the subscription term, multiplied by the amount paid. The reader does not receive a refund for issues already delivered, even if those issues were not read.

23.13 Where a refund is approved for a digital access pass, the refund is calculated on a pro-rata basis using the number of unused days remaining, divided by the total number of days in the pass term. Where the pass has been activated but not used, the full amount is refunded.

**24. Complaint handling – general procedure**

24.1 This section applies to all complaints received by the newspaper, whether by telephone, in writing, by email, or through the online contact form. It does not apply to requests for refunds, which are dealt with under section 23, except where a refund is requested as part of a wider complaint.

24.2 A complaint is defined as an expression of dissatisfaction with the newspaper’s products, services, or staff, where a response is expected. A query about billing or delivery is not a complaint unless the reader states that they are dissatisfied.

24.3 All complaints must be logged on the day they are received. The log must include the reader’s name, contact details, the date of the complaint, the nature of the complaint, and the name of the staff member who took the initial call or opened the correspondence. Where a complaint arrives by email, the email itself must be saved to the reader’s account file, and a note added to the CRM.

24.4 The initial response to a complaint must be sent within 2 business days of receipt. This response should acknowledge the complaint, confirm that it has been logged, and give the name and contact details of the person handling it. The response does not need to resolve the complaint, but it must not promise a resolution date that cannot be met.

24.5 Complaints should normally be resolved within 10 business days of receipt. Where this is not possible, the reader must be told why, and given a revised date. The revised date must be no more than 20 business days from the original receipt date, unless the complaint is subject to an external investigation (for example, by the police or a regulator).

24.6 **Escalation.** If a complaint has not been resolved to the reader’s satisfaction after the initial response, the reader may ask for it to be escalated. Escalation requests must be passed to the Reader Services Manager within 1 business day. The Reader Services Manager will review the case file and respond within 5 business days. Where the complaint concerns a charge of more than £100, or where the reader has made a formal request for compensation, the escalation must be reviewed by the Head of Billing personally.

24.7 Where a complaint is upheld, the newspaper will offer an appropriate remedy. This may include an apology, a correction, a refund, a credit, or a combination of these. The remedy offered should be proportionate to the harm caused and should take into account the reader’s preferences where practical.

24.8 Where a complaint is not upheld, the reader must be told why, and reminded that they may refer the matter to the Independent Press Standards Organisation (IPSO) if they remain dissatisfied. This reminder must be included in the final response letter or email.

**25. Refunds**

25.1 Refunds are available for the following:

- Unused portion of a subscription where the reader has given notice to cancel. Refund is calculated pro-rata from the date of cancellation request, not the date of the final issue.
- Duplicate payment, where a reader has been charged twice for the same product or period in error.
- Payment taken after a cancellation request was received and confirmed by the Billing Department.
- A product or service that was not delivered and where the failure was on our side (for example, a paper not delivered for three or more consecutive days without prior notice of a service change).
- A product or service that was materially different from that described at point of sale, and where the reader has returned or rejected the product within 14 days.

25.2 Refunds are not normally available for:

- Change of mind, where the product or service was delivered as described. An exception may be made within 14 days of the first payment for a new subscription, at the discretion of the Reader Services Manager.
- Delivery failures caused by the reader (for example, an incorrect address supplied, or a holiday hold not requested).
- Editorial content complaints, unless the complaint is upheld under Section 24 of this procedure and a refund is deemed an appropriate remedy.
- Temporary price changes for special editions or supplements, where the price was advertised at the point of sale.

25.3 Refund amounts are calculated before any credit or voucher is applied. Where a reader has already received a credit for the same period, the refund will be reduced by the value of that credit.

25.4 Refunds are paid by the same method used for the original payment wherever possible. Cheque refunds are issued for payments made by cheque or where the original card has expired and no alternative card is held on file. Cheque refunds may take up to 28 days to arrive.

25.5 Refunds of £10 or less may be issued as a credit to the reader’s account instead of a payment, unless the reader specifically requests a payment. This is to avoid bank charges that would otherwise reduce the value of the refund.

25.6 All refunds of £50 or more must be authorised by the Head of Billing or, in their absence, the Deputy Head of Billing. Refunds of £200 or more require the authorisation of the Finance Director. This authorisation must be recorded on the reader’s account file with the date and the name of the authorising officer.

25.7 Where a refund is approved as part of an upheld complaint, the refund decision is recorded in the complaint log and the reader is notified in the final response letter. The refund itself is processed by the Billing Department within 5 business days of the final response being sent.

25.8 **Duplicate payments.** Where a reader reports a duplicate payment, the Billing Department will verify the transactions on the account. If the duplicate is confirmed, the refund is processed automatically without the need for a formal complaint. The reader should be told the expected timescale for the refund to appear on their statement.

25.9 **Direct Debit refunds.** Refunds for Direct Debit payments are returned to the reader’s bank account via the Direct Debit scheme. The reader does not need to contact their bank. The refund will normally appear within 5–10 business days of the refund being processed.

**1. Purpose and scope**

1.1 This procedure sets out how the company handles complaints from readers, how complaints are recorded and escalated, and the circumstances in which refunds may be offered. It applies to all staff who have contact with readers, including the newsroom, circulation, and billing teams.

1.2 The policy covers complaints about:

- Billing errors and charges
- Delivery problems, including missed or damaged papers
- Editorial content and accuracy
- Reader competitions and promotions
- The conduct of staff
- Any other matter relating to the supply of our services

1.3 Complaints about editorial content are handled in the first instance by the newsroom under the Editors' Code of Practice. This policy applies where the complaint relates to service, billing, or the way a reader has been treated. Where a complaint raises both editorial and service matters, the service elements are dealt with under this procedure and the editorial elements are referred to the newsroom.

**2. Definitions**

2.1 **Reader:** Any person who receives our publications, whether by subscription, single-copy purchase, or free distribution.

2.2 **Complaint:** An expression of dissatisfaction, however made, about the standard of service, billing, or conduct of the company or its staff, where a response is expected.

2.3 **Enquiry:** A request for information or a routine request for action that does not express dissatisfaction. Enquiries are not logged as complaints unless the reader indicates they are dissatisfied with the response.

2.4 **Vulnerable reader:** A reader who, because of age, disability, illness, or personal circumstances, may require additional support or a different method of communication. Staff should use their judgement and record any vulnerability noted during contact.

**3. How complaints may be made**

3.1 Complaints may be made by telephone, in writing, by email, through the website contact form, or in person at our offices. Complaints may also be made through social media, although readers are encouraged to provide a contact email or telephone number so that we can respond fully.

3.2 There is no charge for making a complaint, and readers are not required to use a particular form. Staff should help readers who have difficulty putting their complaint in writing, for example by taking details over the telephone and sending a written summary for confirmation.

Delivery and billing complaints are handled by James Okafor, Senior Reader Services Advisor. James handles escalations for delivery and billing complaints. If a reader is not satisfied after you have explained the position, or if the complaint involves a repeated issue (for example, three missed deliveries in a month), do not keep trying to resolve it yourself. Log it as an escalation in the CRM and route it to James’s queue. He works Monday to Friday, 08:30–17:30, and is usually on the desk by 08:45.

Do not escalate the following without checking first:

- A single missed delivery where the reader has not previously complained. Offer a replacement copy and note the delivery route for the next day.
- A billing query where the reader has simply not received an invoice. Re-send the invoice and note the date.
- A direct debit query that is about timing, not an amount. Explain the collection cycle.

Escalate when:

- The reader has complained twice or more about the same issue within 30 days.
- The complaint involves a charge the reader says they never agreed to.
- The reader has asked to speak to a manager or to “someone senior”.
- The complaint is about a delivery that was left in an unsafe place, or not left at all, and the reader has said they do not want it left there again.

When you log an escalation, include the reader’s account number, the date of the original issue, and a one-line summary of what has been tried so far. Do not write “see previous notes” – James will not chase them.

James aims to respond to escalations within two working days. If he is on leave, his queue is covered by the Team Lead. If the Team Lead is also away, the Saturday supervisor checks the queue on Saturday morning.

8. The CRM and note-taking

Always log a note for every reader interaction, including calls that are just a question. If a reader asks something and you answer it, log it. If you do not log it, it did not happen.

Notes should be short and factual. Write in plain English. Acceptable shorthand: “cust called re: delivery”, “re-sent invoice”, “left VM”. Avoid long sentences and avoid copying out the whole conversation. The note is for the next person who picks up the case, not for the archive.

James Okafor handles escalations for delivery and billing complaints. Record status: current.

Use the following fields on every note:

- Reader name and account number
- Date and time
- Reason for contact
- Action taken
- Any promise made (and the date of that promise)

Do not use the notes field for opinions about the reader. Do not write “reader was rude” or “reader seems confused”. If behaviour is a problem, speak to the Team Lead separately.

When you change a reader’s delivery details, always put “CHANGED” in capital letters at the start of the note. When you re-send an invoice, put “RE-SENT” at the start. This makes it easier to scan.

If you make a mistake in a note, do not delete it. Add a new note saying “correction to note dated [date] – [what was wrong]”. The CRM keeps a history and we need to see what happened.

9. Payments and cheques

We accept cheques, card payments over the phone, and bank transfers. We do not accept cash at the desk. If a reader insists on paying cash, direct them to the main office in town (open 09:00–16:30, Monday to Friday) or explain that they can pay by bank transfer.

Cheques are logged on the day they arrive. Write the amount and the account number on the back of the cheque before you log it. Cheques are banked on Tuesdays and Thursdays. If a cheque arrives after 15:00, it is banked on the next banking day.

When a reader queries a charge, do not offer a refund or a credit without checking the account first. Most queries are about the date of a charge or a misunderstanding about the subscription period. If the reader is right and the charge is wrong, log a credit request and the Team Lead will approve it. Do not process credits yourself.

**10. Shift patterns**

The standard working week runs Monday to Friday. Office hours are 09:00–17:30, with a one-hour lunch break. The team operates a rolling rota for lunch so that the phone line is covered between 12:30 and 14:00.

There are three main shifts:

Shift preferences are reviewed twice a year, in January and July. Requests for a permanent change of shift must be submitted to the Team Lead before the 15th of the month preceding the review. The rota is confirmed two weeks before it starts.

Saturday cover is provided on a volunteer basis, one person per week, 09:00–13:00. Saturday work is paid at the overtime rate. If no one volunteers, the Team Lead assigns the cover in rotation. The Saturday rota runs four weeks at a time.

**11. Annual leave and holiday requests**

Annual leave runs from 1 April to 31 March. The leave year matches the financial year, not the calendar year. Your entitlement is shown on your contract; if you are unsure, ask the Team Lead or check the HR portal.

Requests must be made on the holiday form in the shared drive, not by email or in person. The form asks for the dates, the reason (optional), and a note of any outstanding cases you are handling. Fill in all three fields. A request without a note of outstanding cases is returned.

We aim to respond to requests within five working days. Requests are approved on a first-come, first-served basis, but we keep a minimum of two people on the core shift at all times. During the county fair week (first full week of September) and the week before Christmas, only one person may be away at any time.

If you are sick during approved leave, tell the Team Lead on your first day of sickness. You do not need to log it in the CRM. The leave is re-credited once you return and provide a fit note if the sickness lasted more than seven days.

Unused leave cannot be carried over unless the Team Lead has agreed it in writing before 31 March. Carry-over is normally limited to five days and must be used by 30 June.

**12. Bank holidays and the office closure days**

The office is closed on the usual English bank holidays. We also close on the afternoon of the last working day before Christmas Eve, at 13:00.

If a bank holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the substitute day is a normal working day unless HR tells us otherwise. The Team Lead sends a reminder the week before.

**13. Training and new starters**

New starters have a two-week induction. In the first week they shadow a named buddy on the core shift. In the second week they take calls with the buddy sitting next to them. After two weeks they are signed off by the Team Lead.

Mandatory training is refreshed every year:

- Data protection refresher (online, 45 minutes, must be completed by 31 March)
- Fire safety briefing (in person, held in April)
- First aid at work (every three years; check your certificate date)

If you miss a training session, you are responsible for booking the catch-up session with the Team Lead. Do not wait to be reminded.

**14. Desk and equipment**

Each member of staff has a named desk in the main office. Desk moves are decided by the Team Lead, usually once a year in October. If you want a different desk, ask before the September team meeting.

**3. Complaint Handling – First Contact**

3.1 All complaints received by the switchboard or the general office line must be logged on the day of receipt using the Complaints Log (Form RS-CL-01). The log records the reader's name, contact details, the date and time of the complaint, the nature of the complaint, and the name of the staff member taking the call.

3.3 The target for first response is two working days from receipt. This response should either resolve the complaint or explain what steps are being taken to investigate it.

3.5 Complaints that cannot be resolved at first contact, or that involve a refund request, must be passed to the Reader Services Team Lead or, in their absence, to the Duty Manager.

**4. Refund Requests – Authority Levels**

4.1 Refund requests are assessed against the circumstances of the complaint and the reader's history with us. The following table sets out the approval authority for refunds. The table is current as of the effective date of this version.

| Refund Amount | Approval Authority | Notes |
|---------------|--------------------|-------|
| Up to 10 GBP | Any member of Reader Services staff | No further authorisation required. Record in the Complaints Log. |
| 10.01 to 50 GBP | Reader Services Team Lead | Must be logged with a reason. |
| Above 50 GBP | Emily Hartley, as Reader Services Team Lead, approves refunds above 50 GBP. Record status: current. | Requires a completed Refund Request Form (RS-RF-02) and a note of the reader's complaint reference. |
| 250 GBP and above | Head of Billing | Requires written summary of the complaint and proposed resolution. |

4.2 For refunds above 50 GBP, the Refund Request Form must be countersigned by the Billing Department after approval. This is to ensure the refund is processed on the next payment run.

4.3 Refunds are paid by the same method as the original payment wherever possible. Cash refunds are only made at the office counter and require a receipt signature.

4.4 No refund will be considered for complaints raised more than 90 days after the incident giving rise to the complaint, unless exceptional circumstances apply. Exceptional circumstances are judged by the Head of Billing.

---

**5. Escalation and Time Limits**

5.1 If a complaint is not resolved within five working days, it is automatically escalated to the Reader Services Team Lead.

5.2 If the complaint concerns a refund of more than 50 GBP, the escalation must include the Refund Request Form and any supporting correspondence.

5.3 The total time to resolve a complaint, from receipt to final response, should not exceed 15 working days. If this cannot be met, the reader must be written to with an explanation and a revised date.

5.4 Complaints that remain unresolved after 15 working days are referred to the Head of Reader Services for a final decision. The reader is informed of this in writing.

---

7.1 The Refund Request Form is available on the shared drive and in the stationery cupboard. Paper copies are acceptable but must be scanned and attached to the Complaints Log entry once completed.

- Reader name and account number;
- Complaint reference number;
- Refund amount (in GBP, to two decimal places);
- Reason for refund;
- Original payment method;
- Date of original payment (if known);
- Signature of the approving authority.

7.4 For refunds above 50 GBP, the form must be countersigned by the Billing Department. The countersignature confirms that the refund will be included in the next payment run. This is a separate step from the approval in Section 4.

**8. Reader Correspondence**

8.1 All written responses to complaints should be on headed paper and include the complaint reference number.

8.2 Responses should be signed by the person who investigated the complaint, not by a generic signature. If that person is unavailable, the Reader Services Team Lead may sign on their behalf and should note this in the file.

8.3 Where a complaint is upheld in part or in full, the response should state clearly what action has been taken and, where applicable, the refund amount and expected payment date.

8.4 Where a complaint is not upheld, the response should explain the reasons and remind the reader of their right to refer the matter to the Independent Press Standards Organisation (IPSO). A leaflet explaining IPSO is available from the counter; a copy should be enclosed with the response.

8.5 Emails are acceptable for readers who have opted in to email correspondence. The same content requirements apply.

---

**9. Exceptions and Special Circumstances**

9.1 The 90-day limit in Section 4.4 may be waived only by the Head of Billing. Requests for a waiver should be made in writing, with the complaint reference number and a short explanation of the exceptional circumstances.

9.2 Where a reader is unable to provide a receipt or bank statement to confirm the original payment, the Billing Department may accept a screenshot of an email confirmation or a copy of the delivery note. This is at the discretion of the Billing Department.

9.3 Complaints received on behalf of a reader by a third party (for example, a family member or a carers' organisation) will be accepted, but the reader's consent must be recorded in the Complaints Log. Verbal consent is acceptable; note the date and the name of the person giving consent.

**10. Response Time Targets**

10.1 The Billing Department will acknowledge every complaint within two business days of receipt. The acknowledgement may be by letter, email, or telephone, and must include the complaint reference number and the name of the person handling the case.

10.2 Complaints Procedure v3 requires_response_within 5 business days. Record status: current. This means that a substantive response — that is, a response which addresses the points raised and states the outcome or the next steps — must be sent within five business days of the complaint being logged. The five-day clock starts on the day the complaint is received by the Billing Department, not the day it was posted or emailed. If the complaint arrives on a weekend or a bank holiday, the clock starts on the next working day.

10.5 If a substantive response is sent on the fifth business day, it must be sent by 4.00 pm. Anything sent after 4.00 pm is treated as having been sent on the next business day for the purpose of the target. This rule exists so that the target is not met in name only, and so that the Reader Services Team can check the log before the end of the day.

10.6 Complaints that are received by telephone are logged on the call. The reader should be given the complaint reference number before the call ends. If the reader calls back and the reference number has been lost, the Billing Department will search the log by name and postcode.

**11. Escalation**

11.1 If the reader is not satisfied with the substantive response, they may ask for the complaint to be escalated to the Head of Billing. This request should be made within 28 days of the date of the substantive response. The Head of Billing will review the case and issue a final response within 10 business days of the escalation request.

11.2 The Head of Billing's decision is final for the purposes of this procedure. The reader is reminded that they may also refer the matter to IPSO at any time, but IPSO will normally expect the newspaper's own procedure to have been followed first.

**12. Refund Policy**

12.1 Refunds are payable where a complaint is upheld in full or in part and the reader has paid for a service that was not provided, or was provided late or in a defective form. Refunds are not payable for complaints about editorial content, such as the accuracy or tone of an article. Those complaints are covered by the Editorial Complaints Procedure, which is separate.

12.2 The following table lists the refund amounts that apply. These amounts are the standard rates. The Head of Billing may authorise a higher amount in exceptional circumstances, but this is rare and must be recorded in the Complaints Log.

| Circumstance | Refund | Conditions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missed delivery of a single issue | Cost of that issue | Proof of purchase required |
| Missed deliveries for three or more consecutive issues | One week's cover price | Applies to the same delivery address |
| Faulty home delivery (e.g., wet paper, torn paper) | Cost of that issue | Reader must report within 48 hours |
| Cancellation within cooling-off period | Full amount paid | See Section 12.4 |
| Service failure of more than 14 days | Pro-rata refund | Calculated from the date of failure |

12.4 The cooling-off period is 14 days from the date the subscription or service was purchased. This applies to new subscriptions purchased online or by phone. It does not apply to single-issue purchases, to renewals, or to subscriptions purchased at a discounted rate with a free gift. If a free gift was included, the value of the gift is deducted from the refund.

**14. Reader Refunds – Payment and Processing**

14.2 A refund is not processed until the reader has returned any free gift that accompanied the subscription, or until the value of the gift has been deducted as set out in Section 12.4. If the gift is returned damaged, the reader is still liable for the full gift value. The Billing Department will write to the reader to confirm the deduction before processing the refund.

14.4 Refunds below £5 are normally credited to the reader's account rather than paid out, unless the reader specifically asks for a cheque. The reader is told of this at the time of the claim. Account credits can be used against the next invoice.

14.5 The Billing Department keeps a Refund Register. Each entry records the reader's name, the reason code, the amount, the date approved, and the method of payment. The register is reviewed monthly by the Head of Billing. Entries are kept for six years.

**15. Complaints Handling – Acknowledgement and Timescales**

15.2 Complaints Procedure v3 requires_acknowledgement_within 2 business days. Record status: current. This is a current requirement and has applied since the procedure was last reviewed in January 2025. The acknowledgement is sent by letter or email and confirms the reference number, the name of the person handling the complaint, and the expected date of the substantive response.

15.4 Complaints that are received on a weekend or a bank holiday are logged on the next working day. For the purposes of the acknowledgement timescale, the next working day is treated as the day of receipt. This is consistent with the definition of working days in Section 2 of this procedure.

15.5 Phone complaints are acknowledged by email unless the reader asks for a letter. If the reader has no email address, the acknowledgement is sent by post. The Reader Services team will also confirm the reference number verbally at the end of the call, but this does not replace the written acknowledgement.

15.6 Where a complaint is received by a member of the editorial staff, that member of staff must pass the complaint to Reader Services on the same day. The complaint is then logged and acknowledged in the usual way. Editorial staff do not issue acknowledgements themselves.

**16. Escalation and Final Response**

16.2 The Head of Billing's decision is final for the purposes of this procedure. The reader is reminded that they may also refer the matter to IPSO, but IPSO will normally expect the newspaper's own procedure to have been followed first.

**17. Complaints Log and Reporting**

17.2 The Head of Billing reviews the Complaints Log monthly. A summary of complaints, including the number received, the number upheld, and the average time to acknowledge, is reported to the General Manager each quarter. The summary does not include reader names.

**18. Refund Policy – Exceptions**

18.2 No refund is given for a complaint about editorial content, including the accuracy or tone of an article. Those complaints are covered by the Editorial Complaints Procedure, which is separate.

18.4 Where a refund is approved, the reader may ask for the refund to be donated to a local charity. The Billing Department will arrange this and will confirm the donation in writing. The reader does not receive a receipt for the donation from the newspaper.

**19. Review of this Procedure**

19.2 Staff are expected to familiarise themselves with this procedure. Questions about the refund amounts or the complaints timescales should be directed to the Head of Billing. Questions about the Editorial Complaints Procedure should be directed to the Readers' Editor.

20.4 Where a refund is approved, the reader may ask for the refund to be donated to a local charity. The Billing Department will arrange this and will confirm the donation in writing. The reader does not receive a receipt for the donation from the newspaper.

20.5 Refunds are paid by the same method the reader used to pay, unless that method has been closed. In that case, a cheque is issued and posted to the address on the account. Cheques are valid for six months from the date of issue.

20.6 The Head of Billing may approve a refund above the scheduled amounts in exceptional circumstances, for example where a reader has suffered a significant loss because of a repeated billing error. Any such approval must be noted in the Complaints Log with a one-line reason.

---

**21. Complaint Escalation to the Press Complaints Commission**

21.1 This section explains when a complaint may be referred to the Press Complaints Commission (PCC).

21.2 The PCC is the independent body that handles complaints about the newspaper's conduct. The PCC will normally expect the reader to have followed this procedure first, and to have given the newspaper a reasonable opportunity to resolve the matter.

21.3 A complaint may be escalated to the PCC if it remains unresolved after 10 business days from the date the complaint was acknowledged. This is the current threshold for escalation, and it applies to all complaints logged under this procedure. The 10 business days are counted from the day after the acknowledgement is sent, not from the day the complaint was received.

Press Complaints Commission complaint_escalation_threshold unresolved after 10 business days. Record status: current.

21.4 The Reader Services team will inform the reader of this threshold when the complaint is acknowledged. The acknowledgement email includes the sentence: "If we have not resolved your complaint within 10 business days, you may refer the matter to the Press Complaints Commission."

21.5 Where a complaint is likely to take longer than 10 business days to resolve, the Reader Services team must contact the reader before the 10th business day to explain the delay and give a revised timescale. This does not stop the clock; the reader may still escalate on the 10th business day if they wish.

21.6 When the reader refers a complaint to the PCC, the PCC will contact the newspaper directly. The Reader Services team must respond to any PCC enquiry within 5 working days of receiving it, and must copy the Head of Billing on the response.

21.7 The PCC will normally expect the newspaper's own procedure to have been followed first. If the reader escalates before the 10 business days have passed, the PCC may return the complaint to the newspaper and ask the reader to continue with this procedure.

21.8 Complaints that are about editorial content, including the accuracy or tone of an article, are not covered by this escalation route. Those complaints are handled by the Editorial Complaints Procedure, which has its own timescales and its own escalation route to the PCC.

---

**22. Complaints Received by Telephone**

22.1 Complaints received by telephone are logged in the same way as complaints received by email or post. The Reader Services team member who takes the call will complete the complaint form during the call, where possible, and will give the reader the reference number before the call ends.

**23. Refund Policy**

23.1 This section sets out the circumstances in which a reader may receive a refund for a product or service purchased from the newspaper. It applies to print subscriptions, single-copy purchases made through our website, digital access passes, and event tickets sold by the newspaper.

23.2 Refunds are not automatic. A reader must request a refund in writing, by email, or by telephone, and must provide the order reference or, where no order reference exists, the name and address used at the time of purchase.

23.3 Refunds are issued to the original payment method wherever possible. Where the original payment method is no longer available, a bank transfer or postal order will be offered. Refunds are not issued in cash.

23.4 The refund policy is reviewed quarterly by the Billing Department. The version in force at the time of purchase is the version that applies to that purchase, regardless of when the refund is requested.

23.5 **Eligibility window.** A reader may request a refund within 14 days from purchase. This window is measured from the date of purchase, not from the date of first delivery or first access. Refund Policy refund_eligibility_days 14 days from purchase. Record status: current. This is the current eligibility period and has been in force since 6 January 2025.

23.6 Requests received after the 14-day window will be considered only in the exceptional circumstances listed in section 23.9. The Billing Department is not obliged to consider late requests and will normally decline them without a full review.

23.8 Where a reader purchases a gift subscription for a third party, the 14-day window starts on the date of purchase, not on the date the recipient begins receiving the newspaper. The purchaser is the person entitled to request a refund.

23.9 **Exceptional circumstances.** The Billing Department may, at its discretion, consider a refund request received after the 14-day window where:

23.10 In exceptional circumstances cases, the reader must provide supporting evidence. The Billing Department will respond within 5 business days of receiving the evidence, either approving the refund, declining it, or asking for further information.

23.11 **Non-refundable items.** The following are not refundable:

- single-copy newspapers purchased from a newsagent or other retail outlet (the retailer's own policy applies);
- postage and packing charges, unless the item was faulty or the newspaper made an error;
- digital access passes that have been activated and used for more than 48 hours;
- event tickets for events that have already taken place;
- competition entries and charitable donations.

23.12 Where a refund is approved for a print subscription, the refund is calculated on a pro-rata basis. The calculation uses the number of undelivered issues remaining on the subscription, divided by the total number of issues in the subscription term, multiplied by the amount paid. The reader does not receive a refund for issues already delivered, even if those issues were not read.

23.13 Where a refund is approved for a digital access pass, the refund is calculated on a pro-rata basis using the number of unused days remaining, divided by the total number of days in the pass term. Where the pass has been activated but not used, the full amount is refunded.

**24. Complaint handling – general procedure**

24.1 This section applies to all complaints received by the newspaper, whether by telephone, in writing, by email, or through the online contact form. It does not apply to requests for refunds, which are dealt with under section 23, except where a refund is requested as part of a wider complaint.

24.2 A complaint is defined as an expression of dissatisfaction with the newspaper’s products, services, or staff, where a response is expected. A query about billing or delivery is not a complaint unless the reader states that they are dissatisfied.

24.3 All complaints must be logged on the day they are received. The log must include the reader’s name, contact details, the date of the complaint, the nature of the complaint, and the name of the staff member who took the initial call or opened the correspondence. Where a complaint arrives by email, the email itself must be saved to the reader’s account file, and a note added to the CRM.

24.4 The initial response to a complaint must be sent within 2 business days of receipt. This response should acknowledge the complaint, confirm that it has been logged, and give the name and contact details of the person handling it. The response does not need to resolve the complaint, but it must not promise a resolution date that cannot be met.

24.5 Complaints should normally be resolved within 10 business days of receipt. Where this is not possible, the reader must be told why, and given a revised date. The revised date must be no more than 20 business days from the original receipt date, unless the complaint is subject to an external investigation (for example, by the police or a regulator).

24.6 **Escalation.** If a complaint has not been resolved to the reader’s satisfaction after the initial response, the reader may ask for it to be escalated. Escalation requests must be passed to the Reader Services Manager within 1 business day. The Reader Services Manager will review the case file and respond within 5 business days. Where the complaint concerns a charge of more than £100, or where the reader has made a formal request for compensation, the escalation must be reviewed by the Head of Billing personally.

24.7 Where a complaint is upheld, the newspaper will offer an appropriate remedy. This may include an apology, a correction, a refund, a credit, or a combination of these. The remedy offered should be proportionate to the harm caused and should take into account the reader’s preferences where practical.

24.8 Where a complaint is not upheld, the reader must be told why, and reminded that they may refer the matter to the Independent Press Standards Organisation (IPSO) if they remain dissatisfied. This reminder must be included in the final response letter or email.

**Version 4.2 – Effective 6 January 2025**

**25. Refunds**

25.1 Refunds are available for the following:

- Unused portion of a subscription where the reader has given notice to cancel. Refund is calculated pro-rata from the date of cancellation request, not the date of the final issue.
- Duplicate payment, where a reader has been charged twice for the same product or period in error.
- Payment taken after a cancellation request was received and confirmed by the Billing Department.
- A product or service that was not delivered and where the failure was on our side (for example, a paper not delivered for three or more consecutive days without prior notice of a service change).
- A product or service that was materially different from that described at point of sale, and where the reader has returned or rejected the product within 14 days.

25.2 Refunds are not normally available for:

- Change of mind, where the product or service was delivered as described. An exception may be made within 14 days of the first payment for a new subscription, at the discretion of the Reader Services Manager.
- Delivery failures caused by the reader (for example, an incorrect address supplied, or a holiday hold not requested).
- Editorial content complaints, unless the complaint is upheld under Section 24 of this procedure and a refund is deemed an appropriate remedy.
- Temporary price changes for special editions or supplements, where the price was advertised at the point of sale.

25.3 Refund amounts are calculated before any credit or voucher is applied. Where a reader has already received a credit for the same period, the refund will be reduced by the value of that credit.

25.4 Refunds are paid by the same method used for the original payment wherever possible. Cheque refunds are issued for payments made by cheque or where the original card has expired and no alternative card is held on file. Cheque refunds may take up to 28 days to arrive.

25.5 Refunds of £10 or less may be issued as a credit to the reader’s account instead of a payment, unless the reader specifically requests a payment. This is to avoid bank charges that would otherwise reduce the value of the refund.

25.6 All refunds of £50 or more must be authorised by the Head of Billing or, in their absence, the Deputy Head of Billing. Refunds of £200 or more require the authorisation of the Finance Director. This authorisation must be recorded on the reader’s account file with the date and the name of the authorising officer.

25.7 Where a refund is approved as part of an upheld complaint, the refund decision is recorded in the complaint log and the reader is notified in the final response letter. The refund itself is processed by the Billing Department within 5 business days of the final response being sent.

25.8 **Duplicate payments.** Where a reader reports a duplicate payment, the Billing Department will verify the transactions on the account. If the duplicate is confirmed, the refund is processed automatically without the need for a formal complaint. The reader should be told the expected timescale for the refund to appear on their statement.

25.9 **Direct Debit refunds.** Refunds for Direct Debit payments are returned to the reader’s bank account via the Direct Debit scheme. The reader does not need to contact their bank. The refund will normally appear within 5–10 business days of the refund being processed.

**Complaints Procedure and Refund Policy**

**Document reference:** BIL-POL-014

**1. Purpose and scope**

1.1 This procedure sets out how the company handles complaints from readers, how complaints are recorded and escalated, and the circumstances in which refunds may be offered. It applies to all staff who have contact with readers, including the newsroom, circulation, and billing teams.

1.2 The policy covers complaints about:

- Billing errors and charges
- Delivery problems, including missed or damaged papers
- Editorial content and accuracy
- Reader competitions and promotions
- The conduct of staff
- Any other matter relating to the supply of our services

1.3 Complaints about editorial content are handled in the first instance by the newsroom under the Editors' Code of Practice. This policy applies where the complaint relates to service, billing, or the way a reader has been treated. Where a complaint raises both editorial and service matters, the service elements are dealt with under this procedure and the editorial elements are referred to the newsroom.

**2. Definitions**

2.1 **Reader:** Any person who receives our publications, whether by subscription, single-copy purchase, or free distribution.

2.2 **Complaint:** An expression of dissatisfaction, however made, about the standard of service, billing, or conduct of the company or its staff, where a response is expected.

2.3 **Enquiry:** A request for information or a routine request for action that does not express dissatisfaction. Enquiries are not logged as complaints unless the reader indicates they are dissatisfied with the response.

2.4 **Vulnerable reader:** A reader who, because of age, disability, illness, or personal circumstances, may require additional support or a different method of communication. Staff should use their judgement and record any vulnerability noted during contact.

**3. How complaints may be made**

3.1 Complaints may be made by telephone, in writing, by email, through the website contact form, or in person at our offices. Complaints may also be made through social media, although readers are encouraged to provide a contact email or telephone number so that we can respond fully.

3.2 There is no charge for making a complaint, and readers are not required to use a particular form. Staff should help readers who have difficulty putting their complaint in writing, for example by taking details over the telephone and sending a written summary for confirmation.
